items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mr. Nellens, the director of the casino happened to be in the hallway of the dressing rooms. He gave Don hell and that killed the chance for us and the band to have a summer season in the casino of Knokke.

ctx.x: The Edouard's band, Don Byas and myself were still doing concerts and in April, we went to Knokke for three days at the casino with a big show. This was the 16th, 17th and 18th. The show included the orchestras of Bernard Hilda and Maurice Toubas. They were both known as high society orchestras in Europe, and we took care of the jazz department. Other acts engaged were the Nicholas Brothers - dance team- Rosario and Antonio, famous Spanish couple, Borrah Minevitch's Harmonica Vagabonds, the well known Bluebell…

The war had not changed naything in Kokke since I was there the summer of 1938. Everything went well until the last night when Don Byas went into one of his acts after the last show. Of course, we all had quite a few drinks and were feeling no pains. I had already left the casino when thiks incident happened, but I was told by one of the musicians that Don was high and in the process of changing his clothes, he decided to chase one of the Bluebell girls that had passed his lodge when the door was open. The big thing in jazz from the 8th of May until the 15th was the jazz festival that Charles Delaunay organized in collaboration with Frank Bauer, Eddie Barclay and Jacques Souplet. Sidney Bechet and Charlie(the Bird) Parker were the stars, but there were other musicians that were already in the limelight, whose names were to become much better known than they were in 1949.
